TR,DF_ADNKS_T06,1.1.title: Number of households by type and provinces
TR,DF_ADNKS_T06,1.1.description: The table includes annual information on the total number of households and the number of households by type at the provincial level since 2014. Household is defined as a person living alone or a group of persons residing in the same address, with or without any kind of kinship. Persons living in collective living quarters (institutional place, worker dormitories, guesthouses, hotels etc.) are excluded. This definition is based on the international household-dwelling concept. Household types are broadly categorized as "One-person households", "One-family households", "Extended-family households" and "Multi-person no-family households".

TR,DF_ADNKS_T07,1.1.title: Number of households by size and type
TR,DF_ADNKS_T07,1.1.description: The table contains annual information on the number of households by type and size for Türkiye total since 2014. Household is defined as a person living alone or a group of persons residing in the same address, with or without any kind of kinship. Persons living in collective living quarters (institutional place, worker dormitories, guesthouses, hotels etc.) are excluded. This definition is based on the international household-dwelling concept. Household types are broadly categorized as "One-person households", "One-family households", "Extended-family households" and "Multi-person no-family households". In addition, one-family households can be further categorized as "Couple without resident children", "Couple with at least one resident child" and "Lone parents with at least one resident child". Furthermore, lone parents with at least one resident child can be further categorized as "Lone fathers with at least one resident child" and "Lone mothers with at least one resident child".

TR,DF_ADNKS_T08,1.1.title: Number of one-family households by type and provinces

Persons living in collective living quarters (institutional place, worker dormitories, guesthouses, hotels etc.) are excluded. This definition is based on the international household-dwelling concept. One-family households are categorized as "Couple without resident children", "Couple with at least one resident child" and "Lone parents with at least one resident child". Furthermore, lone parents with at least one resident child can be further categorized as "Lone fathers with at least one resident child" and "Lone mothers with at least one resident child".

TR,DF_ADNKS_T36,1.1.title: Population by urban-rural classification, age group and sex
TR,DF_ADNKS_T36,1.1.description:
The table contains annual information on population size by age group, sex and urban-rural classification for Türkiye total as of 2022. Age groups are given in five-year intervals up to 90+.  The new urban-rural classification put forward by the European Statistical Office and categorized as "densely populated, intermediate-density and thinly populated" is based on the "Degree of Urbanisation (DEGURBA)". The classification shows the rural-urban class of an area based on population density over 1 km2 population grids. As data sources, Spatial Address Registration System (SARS) and Address Based Population Registration System (ABPRS) dated 31 December were used.
According to the classification, densely populated areas are defined as quarters and villages that have at least 50 % of their population living in urban centre grids. Intermediate density areas are quarters and villages that do not meet the criteria of densely populated areas and thinly populated areas. Thinly populated areas are quarters and villages that have more than 50% of their population living in rural grid cells. Following the determination of rural-urban class of quarters and villages, population of provinces and districts according to the new urban-rural classification are obtained through aggregation.

As data sources, Spatial Address Registration System (SARS) and Address Based Population Registration System (ABPRS) dated 31 December were used.
According to the classification, densely populated areas are defined as quarters and villages that have at least 50 % of their population living in urban centre grids. Intermediate density areas are quarters and villages that do not meet the criteria of densely populated areas and thinly populated areas. Thinly populated areas are quarters and villages that have more than 50% of their population living in rural grid cells. Following the determination of rural-urban class of quarters and villages, population of provinces and districts according to the new urban-rural classification are obtained through aggregation.
